name: bk_exp10_tost_power
title: 240 passages are enough to call line position flat; direction-to-direction noise caps power that more items cannot lift
caption: Simulated power (2,000 experiments per point, K = 100 random directions per band, inputs bootstrapped from the 60-passage pilot) for the pre-registered equivalence test that Oracle Lens's five descriptive families are flat against both random-direction bands. Shading: Wilson 95% Monte Carlo interval. With no true effect power is 1.00 from n = 120; if the real direction behaves like a random one (violet) power plateaus near 0.93, and lower under the two sensitivity runs (pale dashed), because the direction-level spread does not shrink with n. Caveat: a simulation from pilot data, not a measurement.
notes: Statistic: per-item paired effect e_i = (LO(+D) - LO(-D))/2 minus the band mean; TOST at +/- delta_f (the shift moving AUROC 0.50 -> 0.55), intersection-union over five families and both bands. Values are the simulation's own outputs (no raw item data involved). Series: {"A0": [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0], "Ahalf": [0.974, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0], "Apilot": [0.652, 0.824, 0.921, 0.968], "B0": [0.887, 0.911, 0.928, 0.934], "B0 nulls at the larger pilot norm": [0.635, 0.669, 0.703, 0.715], "B0 direction spread x 1.3": [0.712, 0.738, 0.772, 0.788]}
